newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, Nov 9 Initial Claims from 328,000; Nov 9 4-Week Average from 330,250; Nov 2 Continued Claims from 2,489,000 and Oct 26 from 2,477,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast jobless claims filings of 332,000 in the November 16 week.
Initial claims in the November 16 week were the highest since July 13, when claims stood at 367,000, the department said.
The department said eight states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended November 9, the latest period for which the data are available.

They were California, with 3,941 new claims; New York, with 2,668; North Carolina, with 2,547; Pennsylvania, with 2,016; Michigan, with 1,822; Louisiana, with 1,697; Minnesota, with 1,092; and Washington, with 1,060.
California reported layoffs in agriculture, North Carolina had layoffs in the transportation equipment industry, while Pennsylvania reported layoffs in the food, construction and service industries.
Michigan and Louisiana both reported layoffs in the automobile industry. Minnesota reported seasonal layoffs in all industries. New York and Washington provided no explanation for the rise in claims.
There were no states reporting decreases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the November 9 week.
